messages:
Maya: Heads-up — customer acme-retail reported a burst of 403s right after a scheduled API key rotation around 03:00 UTC. They say identical requests alternate between 200 and 403 with an error body mentioning 'role_mismatch'. They rolled the rotation across regions with ~2m stagger.

Maya: Ticket: https://support.redwood.ai/tickets/4521 — customer pasted curl traces and logs showing the flip/flop.

Sahil: @alex @mira can you triage? sounds like revocation/propagation race or sidecar secret cache.

incidents-bot: Alert created #4521 — elevated 403 rate on /v1/generate for org=acme-retail (reason=role_mismatch).

Alex: grabbing proxy + auth logs now. can someone drop the sample response payload here?

Maya: customer payload: ```
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
{
  "error": "permission_denied",
  "reason": "role_mismatch",
  "detail": "client key no longer matches assigned role id"
}
```
They also included repeated curl calls where alternating attempts return 200/403.

Mira: I pulled Vault audit trail during the window. Rotation job writes new secret metadata, then a KV write updates role_id. Our custom replication job is staggered region-to-region. Some sidecars still had the old secret in their local cache (TTL=5m) and kept signing with the old role id. When auth-service validates, the key_id matched but role_id didn't — hence role_mismatch 403.

Sahil: to confirm, auth checks both key_id and role_id mapping. If role_id flips before consumers rotate, the same key_id can be tied to a new role_id and cause mismatch. consistent with staggered rollout.

Alex: I reproduced locally by simulating a 2-region rollout and sidecar cache. Repro steps:
1) kv write secret/data/api/keys/orgX -> update role_id
2) don't restart sidecars
3) send identical requests -> sometimes 200, sometimes 403

Local logs: ```
auth-service: verify_token: key_id=abc123 role_id=RID-42 -> ok
auth-service: verify_token: key_id=abc123 role_id=RID-43 -> mismatch -> 403
sidecar: using cached token key_id=abc123 role_id=RID-43 (cache-age=00:02:30)
```

Mira: replication ordering allowed metadata to flip on primary before secondaries pulled the updated secret. That left some compute nodes with stale secret state.

Maya: customer asked for immediate mitigation options. They can restart pods to force secret reload or invoke an internal endpoint if available.

Sahil: immediate mitigations we suggested: 
- Restart sidecars/workers (kubectl rollout restart deploy/<svc> or restart pods)
- If they run our sidecar with the internal API, call POST /internal/invalidate-secret-cache {"org":"acme-retail"}

Alex: long-term fixes proposed: 
- Make rotation atomic from client POV: write new key under /pending/<org>, propagate, then atomically rename to /active/<org>.
- Introduce a short grace window where auth-service will accept old->new mappings for N seconds.
- Emit cache-invalidation webhook from rotation controller to pods so sidecars proactively drop caches.
- Lower sidecar cache TTL or make it reactive to rotation events.

Mira: we already have a grace_window setting but acme-retail had it set to 0. For safety we should default to 60s. Also adjust replication/backoff so metadata flips don't outrun secret propagation.

Alex: quick prototype: auth-service will consult a pending_role_map for last 120s on mismatch and accept valid transitional mappings. Will open PR for review.

Sahil: for this incident let's run this runbook: 
- Ask customer to restart sidecars (they did).
- Pause further rotations for org until hotfix lands.
- Deploy auth-service hotfix to accept pending mappings for 2 minutes.
- Update rotation-controller to write pending entries and flip pointer atomically.

Maya: told customer we've paused rotations for their org and requested they restart. They replied: "Restarting now, will update in ~5m".

(5m later)

Maya: customer reports error rate dropped from ~15% to ~0.3% after restart.

Alex: pushed prototype to staging: auth-service consults pending_role_map. Integration tests green. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/auth-service/pull/789

Mira: rotation-controller change: write to /pending/<org> then rename to /active/<org>. Also adding a cache-invalidation webhook.

Sahil: follow-ups: 
- Add alerting when rotation controller writes metadata without triggering invalidate webhook.
- Update docs runbook for customers: recommended restart steps and invalidate endpoint.
- Change default grace_window to 60s and document tradeoffs.

Maya: updating ticket #4521 with mitigation and ETA ~3h for hotfix. Customer requested a postmortem when complete.

Alex: coordinating deploy with Mira to ensure propagation order is correct in staging before prod.

Mira: I'll add the kube commands and invalidate endpoint snippet to the runbook and schedule a brief knowledge-share with SRE on rotation ordering.

Maya: thanks all — closing the incident thread here and assigning PM for postmortem. :thumbsup:

-- end of thread --
